## Setup, global objects and dependencies

```{r}
#| label: packages

if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
   dplyr
  ,dbplyr
  ,glue
  ,tidyverse
  ,gt
  ,ggplot2
  ,labelled
  ,sjlabelled
  ,hablar
  ,janitor
  ,scales
  )

pacman::p_load_gh("actepi/actepir")

# Non-default packages in use, for the dependency statement below
packs_loaded <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, sessionInfo()$otherPkgs))
packageslist <- as.data.frame(installed.packages()[, c(1, 3)]) |>
  dplyr::filter(Package %in% rownames(packs_loaded)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pl = paste0(Package, " (", Version, ")")) |>
  dplyr::pull(pl)

rm(packs_loaded)
```

All analysis is performed in RStudio. Several R packages are also used to
perform and enhance analysis and presentation and, as such, create dependencies
for future replication. For transparency, the non-default packages used were as
follows: `r I(toString(packageslist))`.

### Data

`episerver_quickconnect()` handles driver selection, Windows authentication and
the connection retry loop, so there is no need to hard-code server details or to
work around the RStudio concurrency bug by hand.

```{r}
#| label: data

dt <- episerver_quickconnect("TABLENAME") |>
  # filter(), select() etc. go here — still a lazy query at this point
  collect_withlabels()
```
